newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BOCK FINALLY CUTS LINKS WITH LONRHO

Former chief executive of Lonrho, Dieter Bock, has finally cut all links with the industrial conglomerate, with a 100 million pounds stg profit following the sale last year of his 18.3 per cent stake to Anglo American. Mr Bock will now join forces with TrizecHahn corporation, the 3 billion dollar US Canadian property company.
-- ANNUAL RISE IN HOUSE PRICES SLIPS TO 6.8 PER CENT

Halifax Building Society reported yesterday that house prices rose by 6.8 per cent in February down on the 7.1 per cent rise it recorded in January. A spokesman for the Halifax said the latest figures show that January's downturn was simply a one-off adjustment for the larger than expected monthly rises at the end of 1996.
-- RATIONALISATION TRIMS BICC PROFITS TO 64 MILLION POUNDS

BICC, the cables and construction group, announced pre-tax profits of 64 million pounds stg last year after an exceptional charge of 65 million pounds stg for rationalisation and property writedowns. Chief executive, Alan Jones, said that capital expenditure in rapidly developing telecommunications and data businesses rose by 40 per cent last year and was expected to rise another 40 per cent in 1997.
THE TIMES
-- LIFE FIRMS WELCOME PENSIONS PROPOSALS

New proposals to privatise pensions have been welcomed by life companies and investment managers who say that the move could lift their annual premium income by hundreds of billions of pounds every year. Privatised pensions are expected to be run by a select group of providers regulated and approved by the Personal Investment Authority, and competition for inclusion in the list will be fierce.
-- CITY STAR AT HEART OF NOMURA INQUIRY

One of the City of London's top stockbrokers may be called to give evidence in connection with a 290 million pounds stg share deal on the Australian Stock Market. The former co-head of equities at Nomura International in London, Robert Mapstone, initiated the arbitrage trade. Nomura is being taken to court by the Australian Securities Commission for alleged market manipulations and trading in securities in which it was both buyer and seller.
-- CADBURY SCHWEPPES READY TO SPEND 2 BILLION POUNDS

Cadbury Schweppes signalled yesterday that it is looking to make a substantial acquisition saying it is ready to spend 2 billion pounds stg if the right opportunity arose. The confectionery and soft drinks group, which last month received 623 million pounds stg from the sale of its stake in its joint distribution venture to Coca-Cola, said it was more likely to add to its confectionery arm with the new money.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CITY TOLD TO CURB BONUSES

The City has been told that it must put a stop to excessive bonuses for dealers or risk having financial penalties imposed by regulators. The Bank of England is thought to be planning to take into account additional financial risks encouraged by the bonus system when it is assessing the capital requirements of the banks it supervises. The Securities and Investments Board is set to call for financial penalties for companies whose remuneration schemes alter their risk profile.
-- BAT CONSIDERS US SETTLEMENT

The tobacco and financial services combine, BAT Industries, is prepared to consider a settlement with US tobacco litigants, if it is in the interest of shareholders, it said yesterday. Chief executive, Martin Brighten, said that it was time to evaluate the possible settlement of a string of US tobacco related legal cases, and that a sensible settlement would be one covering all current and future claims approved by Congress and the White House.
-- JOBS GO AT FIRM HIT BY ASBESTOSIS

T&N is to cut 2,500 jobs due to the cost of setting up a 1 billion pounds stg safety net to meet potential asbestosis claims last year. The Manchester based engineering and car parts company, once Britain's biggest asbestos producer, fell from a 120 million pounds stg profit to a 388 million pounds stg loss following a charge of 500 million pounds stg which the company hopes will cover future and current claims from asbestosis sufferers.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- ANDERSEN CONSULTING REVENUES AT RECORD 5 BILLION DOLLARS

Andersen Consulting 's annual revenues were boosted to a record 5.3 billion dollars US last year as the growing trend for businesses to outsource non-core activities continued. Business process management or outsourcing was the area with the biggest rise, with fees going up 46 per cent to 582 million dollars US in the year to 31 December 1996. The company is moving away from straightforward information technology services towards helping organisations with many non-core activities.
-- GRID APPEALS ON PENSION RULING

National Grid appealed to the High Court yesterday against a ruling by the Pensions Ombudsman to return 46.3 million pounds stg of surplus cash removed from its pension fund. The Ombudsman had ruled last month that the Grid had mis-used the money which was part of a 62.3 million pounds stg surplus discovered in 1992. A preliminary application to postpone the settlement could take place before the end of the group's accounting year at the end of March.
-- FRENCH HOTEL GROUP TO SELL 260 MILLION POUNDS STAKE IN COMPASS

French hotel group, Accor, announced yesterday that it plans to sell half of its 21.5 per cent stake in the catering company Compass. The sale, to cut Accor's debts, should raise around 260 million pounds stg, and is going ahead with the full knowledge and permission of Compass's management. Shares in Compass fell by 3.7 per cent to 713.75 after the announcement.
